transcript: You only have through this weekend to get yourself up to Harlem to catch a free production of Memnon in Marcus Garvey Park. This play, being presented by the Classical Theatre of Harlem, tells the story of the titular Ethiopian king Memnon who comes back to Troy in its time of need during the Trojan War. Throughout the play, Memnon and other characters like Achilles and Helen each wrestle with a lot of internal conflict, questioning the expectations that have been put on them in a time of such violence and chaos. Most significantly, Memnon feels rightfully hesitant about fighting on behalf of a place where he has historically always been othered, being only half-Trojan. The themes of duty, identity, and legacy shine through in this production, and although this play has a lot of exposition, it also offers some really stunning fight sequences, lavish costumes and projections, and of course great performances. At a tight 80 minutes, and on a night that had perfect weather for some outdoor theatre, I found this to be a really nice experience, as did the rest of the very full audience that night. With that, another program for my collection.
